name: The blasphemer in the camp
charge: Blaspheming the Name in a quarrel
summary: In a fight within the camp, a man blasphemed the Name and cursed. He was held until the Lord's mind was made known, and his case set the statute for all Israel.
offense: He is identified by his lineage before his act, and the lineage is the first thing the case teaches. The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and this son of the Israelitish woman and a man of Israel strove together in the camp (Leviticus 24:10). His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan (Leviticus 24:11), so the mother was named and the tribe was named, and he was conceived in Egypt while Israel dwelt among the Egyptians; there is no half Israel, and he was counted with his mother's people. In the strife the Israelitish woman's son blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed (Leviticus 24:11). The offence was against God directly, in the camp, spoken aloud and heard.
judgment: The Lord commanded that the whole congregation stone him outside the camp, the witnesses laying their hands on his head. From his case came the law: whoever blasphemes the Name shall be put to death.

entries.commentary: The children of Israel were commanded to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Aaron ordered it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually, upon the pure candlestick, a statute for ever in your generations.

Twelve cakes of fine flour were set in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord, with pure frankincense upon each row, every sabbath, taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in the holy place, for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the Lord made by fire.

The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and strove in the camp with a man of Israel, and blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. They put him in ward, that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them; and the Lord commanded that he that had cursed be brought forth without the camp, that all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and that all the congregation stone him. The strife in the camp likely arose from a man of Israel correcting him concerning the law. His father being an Egyptian shows he was conceived while Israel was in captivity in the land of Egypt, dwelling among the Egyptians; in the same way Moses, outside of Egypt with Jethro the priest of Midian, took a wife there. And there is no such thing as being half Israelite or a fourth Israelite: if your parent is Israel, you are Israel. Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin, and he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, he shall surely be put to death, as well the stranger as he that is born in the land.

He that killeth any man shall surely be put to death, and he that killeth a beast shall make it good, beast for beast. If a man cause a blemish in his neighbour, as he hath done, so shall it be done to him: breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. One manner of law stood for the stranger as for one of your own country. When Christ came he taught the proper understanding of eye for eye for dealing inside the nation: ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth, but I say unto you that ye resist not evil. As the Son of God he had authority to magnify the law: whosoever smites thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also; if any man sue thee and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also; whosoever compels thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience, and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

verses.text: And the son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel: and this son of the Israelitish woman and a man of Israel strove together in the camp;
And the Israelitish woman’s son blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. And they brought him unto Moses: (and his mother’s name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan:)
And they put him in ward, that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Bring forth him that hath cursed without the camp; and let all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin.

And he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, he shall surely be put to death, and all the congregation shall certainly stone him: as well the stranger, as he that is born in the land, when he blasphemeth the name of the Lord, shall be put to death.
And Moses spake to the children of Israel, that they should bring forth him that had cursed out of the camp, and stone him with stones. And the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses.
Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
